reason: This plugin is best classified as automation tooling for local development operations: it integrates a DSH web panel and agent-facing tools to discover/register services, manage start-stop-restart actions, and coordinate service metadata through a shared local registry with port conflict handling. Risk is moderate because it can launch/stop local processes and writes control state/logs, but it appears scoped to local project service management rather than remote system administration.

summaries.zh: 这是一个 DeepSeek Harness 本地服务控制插件，可通过 Web 面板和工具统一进行项目服务的登记、启动、停止、重启及日志查看，并结合端口规则进行协同管理。
summaries.en: This is a DeepSeek Harness local service control plugin that lets users and agents manage projects through a web panel and tools, including registering services, starting/stopping/restarting them, and handling port conflicts with shared local state.

capabilities: Start, stop, restart, and restart-status local services
Detect and register services from project configuration files
Manage a cross-project service registry and persist service metadata/log paths
Arbitrate port conflicts and rewrite launch arguments for alternative ports
Expose RPC endpoints consumed by the web client for control actions

reasons.code: The host component explicitly defines service lifecycle tools (start/stop/restart/status) and process management behavior, including detached startup and recursive termination logic.
The UI client provides a floating service panel with one-click controls and expandable logs for each service.
A global registry file is used (service-registry.json) and includes runtime fields like pid and actualPort, indicating persistent local process/state control.
The plugin declares a web host/client entry model in package metadata (dsh bundle + web client) and exports host/client modules.
Control requests are sent via HTTP RPC (`/service-deck/rpc`) with host-injected token, so runtime command inputs can reach host-side execution paths.
